text: Team stats: both sides are built the same way, from play-by-play box scores rather than a scouting report, so they compare like with like. Their figures cover only the games before this matchup.

The brief shows the 6 highest-priority of 15 keys; every key is on the app. Each key is scored 0-100: who says so (staff-written keys score highest), how big the edge is, how much data backs it, and whether it is an instruction. Keys scoring 55+ are shown, best first, up to 6, one per topic. Keys are built by the parser into uww_ktv_keys.csv and rendered identically by the app. Each key's evidence (the numbers behind it) and full reasoning are on the app's Keys to Victory tab -- click a key to open it there. HOW "FEATURE THE ... COMBO" IS CHOSEN: every 3-player group from our lineup stints, counting competitive minutes only -- a stint that starts in the 2nd half or OT with the margin at 15+ is garbage time and set aside. A trio needs 40+ competitive minutes across 3+ games. It is ranked by scoring margin per 40 minutes, shrunk toward zero as if 40 more minutes of an even game were added, so a short hot streak can't top the list. It must also be on/off positive: we do better with those three on the floor than with them off, which separates the trio from whoever else was out there. If no trio clears all of that, there is no combo key -- a missing key means none qualified yet, not that it wasn't checked. When the top trio has numbers identical to other trios (they only ever played together as one group), no single trio can be singled out, so the key names the whole group as a "unit" instead. Season-wide, not specific to this opponent. REBOUNDING KEYS: "box out" when they rebound 35%+ of their own misses, "crash the glass" when they secure 65% or less of opponents' misses, each on 20+ paired misses from their play-by-play.

WHEATON (IL) starters: started 2+ of the last 3 game(s). Per-game averages from their own film. After each bio: 'Off' = his offensive role (BBall Index's 12) from his play types; 'Def' = his defensive role (BBall Index's 7) from coverage tags with his number, film tracking where he was identified for sure, and his steals/blocks -- '(low sample)' when there's little to go on, '(position only)' with no data. Photo, jersey, position, height and class come from the FastScout roster page when a live scrape has run; hand and status aren't on that page and stay blank. Coach notes pass through as written; data-driven lines are stated against the team's own averages with attempt floors. 🎥 lines are from player tracking on 244 tracked clip(s) of Wheaton (IL) Thunder: who he guarded most, how far off his man he plays, how he plays screens and who he screens for. Only once tracking names players on 50%+ of their floor spots, and never from a player it couldn't name; names on film are partly best guesses until the coaches' player checks confirm them. Approximate feet, small sample.

Their best three five-man units and best three 3-man combos, ranked by scoring margin per 40 minutes, shrunk toward zero as if 40 minutes of an even game were added, so a short hot stretch can't top the list. A five-man unit needs 8+ minutes and a combo 12+; * marks a unit shown below that floor because fewer than three cleared it. Includes all minutes: their lineup data has no score at the start of each stint, so garbage time can't be set aside. A combo's minutes are every stint with all three on the floor, whoever the other two were. GP isn't shown for their combos: games played can't be counted exactly from their lineup data. The key shown is the first data-driven key for that unit. "What they run" is the sets tagged on possessions with that exact five on the floor, and "Group" is its position shape (3G-2B = three guards and two bigs, from roster positions). Every lineup's full strengths, weaknesses and keys are in the app.

🎥 From the film: player tracking on 244 tracked clip(s) of Wheaton (IL) Thunder. Each tracked screen's coverage is the coaches' tag when the clip has one, else tracking's own estimate (marked *: stayed attached vs went under / behind). Defenders who play it differently need tracking to name players first. Small sample -- a lead to check on film.

Every row here is the defense the opponent's offense FACED on a tagged possession, so it reads as how they did against that look -- not what they run on defense themselves. Man, Zone and Press are families, not specific coverages: at this sample size a named coverage is a handful of clips. PPP is points per tagged possession. Treat these as things to CONFIRM on film, not as settled reads -- the clip count on each row is how much weight it carries.

A team that gets the ball with about 0:35-1:00 left in a half can shoot early on purpose: the other team then has to shoot before the horn, and the first team gets the last shot -- two possessions to one. NCAA men's rules (30-second shot clock, 20 after an offensive rebound). The chance is the first possession of the half that starts in that window; went for it = first shot, free-throw trip or turnover with 0:33+ left; got it = a second real possession (3+ seconds) and more trips than the other team. End of the 2nd half / overtime counts only for a team that's behind -- ahead or tied, teams hold for the last shot. Possessions are rebuilt from every game's play-by-play (no possession column exists), so every half on file counts, not just tagged clips. Play calls appear once the coaches have tagged 2+ end-of-half possessions with one; until then it's Synergy's play type. Who to attack weighs foul rate (box scores), fouls while defending 2-for-1 possessions, defensive role and how often he's on the floor at the end of a half.

🎥 From the film: player tracking on 244 tracked clip(s) of Wheaton (IL) Thunder. Recurring alignments are the same spots on the floor seen again and again (drawn in the app); inbounds are grouped by situation. Court pictures (shot chart, screen spots, play diagrams) only once the court mapping passes the film-quality check. Small sample -- a lead to check on film.

UW-WHITEWATER starters: started 2+ of the last 3 game(s). Per-game averages from their own film. After each bio: 'Off' = his offensive role (BBall Index's 12) from his play types; 'Def' = his defensive role (BBall Index's 7) from coverage tags with his number, film tracking where he was identified for sure, and his steals/blocks -- '(low sample)' when there's little to go on, '(position only)' with no data. Flags come from our own season film (highest-confidence first in the app). Play-call lines need 3+ tagged uses of a set.

Our best three five-man units and best three 3-man combos this season, from the play-by-play's lineup stints, ranked by scoring margin per 40 minutes shrunk toward zero as if 40 minutes of an even game were added. Competitive minutes only: MIN and +/- leave out stints that start in the 2nd half or later with the margin already lopsided. A five-man unit needs 8+ minutes; a combo meets the same bar as the "Feature the ... combo" key (40+ minutes, 3+ games, better with them on than off), so that combo is the top row. * marks a unit shown below the bar because fewer than three cleared it. PPP is offense only, from tagged possessions, and does not affect the order.

Same tagged possessions as HOW WE RUN OFFENSE above, sorted by how often we call a set against how well it scores. The usage line is the median (5 uses) and the efficiency line is our own average (0.98 PPP), so this is relative to us, not to the league. Sets with fewer than 3 tagged possessions are left out -- not enough reps to judge. Read it as a call sheet, not a verdict: a low-efficiency set may still be there to set up something else. Reads: from the coaches' Film Tagging -- for each action in a play, what the ball handler / trigger did (use, reject or split the ball screen, Cobra, Fox, ...) and what the screener did after (roll, pop, slip). Share = of that player's reads of that action. A play's points are credited to every action in it. Players with 2+ uses of a read.
